options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Shortest Distance Between Skew Lines (Vectors and Three-Dimensional Geometry):
Passing points: $\vec{a}_1 = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{a}_2 = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$[cite: 4].
$\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1 = (2-1)\hat{i} + (4-2)\hat{j} + (5-3)\hat{k} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$.
Direction vectors: $\vec{b}_1 = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}_2 = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$[cite: 4].
Compute $\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2$:
$\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2 = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \end{vmatrix}$
$= \hat{i}(15 - 16) - \hat{j}(10 - 12) + \hat{k}(8 - 9) = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$.
Magnitude: $|\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2| = \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 2^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 1} = \sqrt{6}$.
Numerator of shortest distance formula:
$|(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2)| = |1(-1) + 2(2) + 2(-1)| = |-1 + 4 - 2| = 1$.
Shortest distance:
$d = \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$[cite: 4].

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
